claims.statement: Key data has one eight-kind declaration, KEY_DATA_SOURCE_DEFINITIONS (derived, contract-term, domain-source, negotiation-source, result-fact, request-input, needs-decision, other), where each entry carries its picker label and a resolved flag; the inspector badge, the ledger and the native key-data audit all read that declaration, and RESOLVED_KEY_DATA_SOURCES is a filter over the same flags rather than a second list.

classifyKeyDataSource is a pure precedence rule over the entity category/kind and the attribute name/derivedByRuleRef: a derivedByRuleRef makes an item derived, otherwise contract attributes are contract-term, Thing attributes domain-source, rfp/proposal attributes negotiation-source, confirmation/other-evidence attributes result-fact, and fulfillment_request attributes request-input when the name is in REQUEST_FORMATION_FIELDS or needs-decision otherwise.

Request attributes count as request-input only when named in the small request-formation whitelist (started_at, request_number, delivery_address, return_address, fault_description, asset_code, billing_period, settlement_period); every other request attribute remains needs-decision.
Every source kind except needs-decision and other counts as resolved, and only needs-decision marks a decision still owed.

The ledger inventories only attributes whose keyData flag is exactly true, so an amount, deadline or quantity that is not marked keyData never enters the decision list and cannot block downstream work.

A derived ledger entry carries its rule id, expression and providers derived from the rule bindings, where each alias resolves either to a modeled ref (with optional cardinality) or to a runtime value type.

The sensor report summarizes the ledger as totalItems, resolvedCount, decisionOwedCount and a capped unresolved list; owed decisions are warnings rather than static errors but keep the stage gate closed.

Each evidence kind mandates business-time attributes (started_at/expired_at for rfp, proposal and request; signed_at for contract; confirmed_at for confirmation; created_at for other evidence), and any recognised time attribute must be a required keyData timestamp.

Lineage requires a many binding to be read through a CEL macro, forbids a macro over a non-many binding, requires an entity binding to use a static string attribute index, and records every read as an entity#attribute access.

Traceability refuses a read of an undeclared attribute, a read whose binding ref differs from the entity, multiple derivation rules targeting one attribute, a derivation target not declared by derivedByRuleRef, and any cycle in attribute lineage.

For a key derived attribute the lineage must reach at least one modeled Entity attribute and may not read a scalar type-only binding, so a formula cannot hide a constant such as a tax rate outside the model.

An entity may carry an optional entity-level sourceSnippet (verbatim sentence, locator, input kind), which compileDraft copies from the draft element's provenance, which the draft review panel prints as 原文 before compile and the workbench projection strips; sourceSnippet is in the entity key set only and no check resolves it against the model.

other is the one kind that is neither resolved nor owed: it never enters the ledger's decisionOwed list, while the sensor summary computes resolvedCount arithmetically as totalItems minus decisionOwedCount, so an unclassified item is counted as resolved in the summary even though isKeyDataResolved returns false for it.

A derivation is recorded on both sides — the attribute's derivedByRuleRef and the rule's target — and strictValidateDomainModel plus analyzeTraceability keep them symmetric through an unresolved-ref check, a mismatch in either direction and an owner-context rule; because classifyKeyDataSource only tests that derivedByRuleRef is present, a dangling ref still classifies as derived even though the model is invalid.

buildKeyDataLedger inventories only attributes whose keyData flag is true, and nothing in strictValidateDomainModel forces that flag onto an amount-like attribute (only the recognised business-time names are forced), so an unmarked amount stays out of the ledger and blocks nothing.

A ledger entry carries the entity identity and category.kind signature, an optional contextRef, the attribute's name/label/meaning/value type, the classified source and decisionOwed; a derived entry adds the rule id, the expression and one provider per binding alias — a modeled ref with optional cardinality, or a runtime valueType with an empty ref — and an unresolvable derivedByRuleRef yields no rule id and no providers.

A key-data source is never written by hand: the inspector badge is read-only over the classification and offers only binding a derivation rule or retracting the claim with keyData false, and the ledger is rebuilt from session.getDocument() on every document change so the badge cannot drift from the model.

An owed key-data decision is a warn-severity KEY_DATA_DECISION_OWED finding rather than a static error: the report keeps passed true and blockCount 0, but isStageGateReady ANDs decisionOwedCount === 0 with the gate summary, block count and API coverage, so owed key data alone keeps the model out of downstream hand-off and the status bar reads 门禁：等待台账决议.

keyDataSummary caps the unresolvedItems list and the per-item findings at MAX_KEY_DATA (40) while decisionOwedCount keeps the full count, so a large decision list is truncated in display but not in the gate arithmetic.

analyzeTraceability enforces the lineage rules (a many binding read only through a CEL collection macro, static string attribute index, declared attributes, binding/attribute match, one derivation per attribute, a derivation target declared back by derivedByRuleRef, no cycles) and adds two key-data rules: a key derived attribute must trace to at least one modeled Entity attribute and may not read a scalar binding the expression uses.

A contract is first annotated into three clause categories (business, domain, boilerplate) that each declare a destination — evidence, domain-thing, none — and annotateContractClauses filters boilerplate first, then a business action, then a computation, reporting the sentences it cannot place; the annotations live only in the reading result, because a compiled model persists sourceSnippet instead of clause buckets.

There is no persisted interview trace: the native sensor set states that the model is its only input, the desktop keeps no interview log (the tool-call activity stream is the record of the conversation), and interview survives only as one value of sourceSnippet.source.
